# Feature: Weight switch — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #29 (Weight switch) from Switches and Doors before it is used in real levels. Effect: needs a block left on it. Unique: a pushed block holds it after the player leaves. Useful: a permanent hold the floor switch cannot give. Source status in the candidate file is 'trial'.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** needs a block left on it.

**So that** a permanent hold the floor switch cannot give.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Weight switch for the first time in its teaching room (mech-29-weight-switch-room). Teaching moment: First room: a weight switch beside its door, with a block in the room. A player who stands on the plate, sees the door open, and steps off to use it watches it close exactly as the floor switch did, which teaches that what this plate wants left on it is the block. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: The plate is only active while a block sits on it (you standing on it works too, but you cannot leave it held)
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Remove the block and the door closes
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: This is the permanent hold the floor switch cannot give

## Edge Cases & Rules

- The plate is only active while a block sits on it (you standing on it works too, but you cannot leave it held)
- Remove the block and the door closes
- This is the permanent hold the floor switch cannot give
- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Weight switch's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Assets & Level Data Needed

- Level JSON: new Test Level mech-29-weight-switch-room (rows + legend) implementing the teaching moment above.
- Sprites/defs: reuse existing tiles where the mechanic reuses an existing tile; add a new sprite/tile def only if this mechanic introduces a new tile (confirm in the implement task).
- Source: plans/level-design/candidate-mechanics/switches-and-doors.yml mechanic #29.
